criterion_name: Precision and rigor in statements and proofs
articulated_construct: Meet community standards of rigor and precision: define terms and conditions exactly, justify every claim with accepted reasoning, use precise terminology, and eliminate ambiguity and errors.

selected_retrospective_seed.role: existing manually selected LaTeX-span capability reused as pipeline input

relation_decomposition.construct_match: An explicitly presented algebraic equality step should preserve the same rational expression on its declared domain.
relation_decomposition.operation: Parse both sides into SymPy rational-expression ASTs, reduce their difference exactly, and enumerate nonzero denominator obligations.
positive_witnesses: exact zero reduced difference certifies equality on the reported denominator-nonzero domain
an exact rational assignment with unequal values certifies nonidentity; it refutes the document only when universal scope is separately supplied
does_not_establish: that the document intended a universal identity rather than a definition or solved special case
branch conditions for roots, logarithms, or transcendental functions
that the surrounding proof is complete or rigorous

relation_decomposition.reason: Whether an equation is universal, conditional, definitional, or evaluated at a special solution requires reading its mathematical role and assumptions.
Accepted reasoning, precise terminology, and completeness are not consequences of algebraic equivalence alone.

coverage_policy.exact_nonidentity_witness: executable relation-local witness with document claim scope unresolved
coverage_policy.universal_identity_counterexample: reserved for an exact nonidentity witness paired with a separately supplied true universal-scope determination

representation.input: sanitized TRAIN ctext only during compilation
representation.authorship_boundary: retrospective-seed procedural blindness; no per-item outcome, heldout, reference, or residual access
